items.title: HELMET: evaluating long-context language models

items.title: The anatomy of harness engineering: behavioral evals for coding agents
items.decision: Catalog-only candidate. Official Google engineering authors describe behavioral evals that assert on intermediate tool calls and file edits, a three-step failure-mode iteration loop, and batch runs over single trials. Distinct from the existing harness entries, which cover harness structure rather than how to test harness changes.
overlap: Harness Design for Long-Running Application Development
Harness Engineering: Leveraging Codex in an Agent-First World
evidence_gaps: Article's Python sample references the Antigravity SDK repository; the repository README shows hooks and policies, not an inspected behavioral-eval module.
No reported experiment or measured result, only a described method.
Page-stated date September 9, 2026; a search result claimed September 11. Page date used.
items.next_action: Before catalog admission, locate the eval code path in google-antigravity/antigravity-sdk-python or confirm the sample is illustrative only, then set topic (Context & Harness vs MLOps & Production), level and audience. No new URL and no required-reading promotion.

items.title: Automation's Early Footprint: where agentic tools actually exist
items.decision: Admitted to the catalog September 15. Dataset verified firsthand: CohereLabs/ate resolves on Hugging Face with a 694k-row onet_matches subset carrying per-pair cosine similarity and good/partial/bad match ratings. The dataset card itself is thin on collection methodology; the article carries it. Filed as Cohere / Research & Economics / deep / founder, the first Cohere entry in the catalog. No curriculum promotion.
evidence_gaps: May 2026 snapshot; counts age even though the method does not.
O*NET matching is LLM-based and carries its own error; nobody here has audited it.
Published by a lab with a commercial position in the agent ecosystem.
items.next_action: Verify on production after deploy. Distribution draft written at distribution/cohere-automation-early-footprint.txt, unsent.

items.title: Orchard: training and evaluating agents inside real harnesses
items.decision: Catalog-only candidate. Microsoft Research describes a Kubernetes-native sandbox for training and evaluating agents inside deployed harnesses rather than simplified stand-ins, with three recipes and reported numbers: Orchard-SWE 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified at ~3B active parameters, Orchard-GUI 68.4% average, Orchard-Claw 59.6%. The repository github.com/microsoft/Orchard resolves and contains trainer and eval code plus published trajectory datasets, so the claimed artifacts verify.
overlap: Harness Design for Long-Running Application Development
Harness Engineering: Leveraging Codex in an Agent-First World
Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
evidence_gaps: Benchmark numbers are self-reported; no third-party reproduction located.
Framework-tied, so shelf life is the weakest of the five gate checks.
Narrower audience than the Agents module average — relevant to people training agents, not everyone building them.
items.next_action: Before catalog admission, decide whether the entry points at the blog post or the repository, and set topic (Agents vs Evals), level (build) and audience. No new URL.

items.title: Testing agent skills systematically with evals
items.decision: Watchlist, not admitted. Teaches an eight-step skill-eval loop with a SKILL.md sample, a Node eval runner and a rubric JSON Schema, but the page carries no publication date and no author byline, which fails the evidence check on its face. Every sample binds to codex exec. The queued Google behavioral-evals article teaches the same run-record-grade loop with a date and named authors.
items.next_action: Revisit only if the page gains a date and byline, or if the deterministic-grader pattern is not adequately covered once the Google candidate is resolved.

items.title: check:guides cannot run without a local dev server
items.decision: Diagnosed during the September 15 scout, not fixed. npm run check:guides fails with ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3019 unless a dev server is already running on that port. That is the script's design — it checks live routes — but it means the check cannot run in a clean checkout or in CI without first starting a server. Low priority; the Guides surface is still local-only.
items.next_action: Owner decision in a production session: either start a server inside the script, fail with a clear message naming the prerequisite, or leave it as a manual-only check. No scout change.
